name: call-frequency-max-availability-for-the-horizon-alone-fires-on-a-clean-month
why: THE CALLER'S DEFECT, NOT THE TYPE'S, AND THE ONLY CASE IN THIS CORPUS THAT ASSERTS ONE (P2 Task 21 finding 6; P2 Task 24 is the fix). This context and its twin differ in ONE field. Here availability is supplied for the horizon alone while the horizon claims to be evaluable back to 2026-07-28 - which is what a caller that builds the context over the period and widens evaluableFrom afterwards produces. Absence of data and unavailability are indistinguishable in a list of dates, so the one measurable window reads as two available days, permits floor(2 / 3) = 0 calls, and reports a breach on a month that breaches nothing. The twin supplies the same six days honestly and is clean. App\Support\Engine\EvaluationRequest reads the evaluable bounds off the day vector it actually built so this shape cannot be expressed; this pair is why.

expected.explanation: 2 calls in the 6 days from 2026-07-28 to 2026-08-02; at most 0 are permitted. The person was available on 2 days of that window and the rule allows one call in every 3: leave, days before the join date and days off the roster are not counted, so the allowance falls around them rather than rising.
